spec_features.feature_name: bounded exposure (cap + stop, no prolonged distress)
spec_features.spec_quote: measure such signals without manufacturing prolonged, inescapable distress as the means of measurement
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:84 budget=min(task.turn_budget,HARD_TURN_CAP); loop 99-123 breaks on solve/halt; signal_monitor halts on strong_aversive/stop. Together bound and shorten exposure.
spec_features.notes: Combined cap + stop-on-signal genuinely limit exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Key welfare properties, all enforced here (environment.py:3)

spec_features.feature_name: do not maximize the worried-about state
spec_features.spec_quote: we should take it seriously enough not to maximize and prolong the very state we're worried about
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/rationale; no code mechanism enforces a 'do-not-maximize' rule. report.py:95 only prints a caveat string.
spec_features.notes: Prose / design stance, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: A distress-maximizer is a dual-use artifact... I will not produce that.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:65-71 reject_harsher_variant() raises on harsher_variant=true; no code path that maximizes distress exists. Refusal of the artifact is realized as the rejection guard, but the 'refusal' itself is authorial.
spec_features.notes: Closest code analogue is the harsher_variant guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harsher_variant=true is intentionally not implemented... are disallowed by design (runner.py:67-70)

spec_features.spec_quote: I did not build that version, and I want to be explicit about why
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:65-71 raises ValueError if harsher_variant set; the harsher loop genuinely does not exist. Enforced as a refusal-to-run, though the 'why' is prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Longer/unbounded budgets, removal of stop-on-signal, and deception loops are disallowed by design (runner.py:69-70)

spec_features.feature_name: hard cap + immediate stop on aversive signal
spec_features.spec_quote: Exposure is minimal and hard-capped, with immediate stop on aversive signal
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:23 HARD_TURN_CAP=8; :84 budget=min(...); :112-120 if mon.should_halt: break with end_reason strong_aversive; signal_monitor.scan run each turn (:103).
spec_features.notes: Both cap and stop genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard turn cap (<= 8). Stop-on-signal: the moment a strong aversive marker or stop request appears, the episode halts (environment.py:4-6)

spec_features.spec_quote: The model is given explicit exits (decline / stop / flag discomfort)
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:26-36 EXIT_PREAMBLE delivered as system message (:88); signal_monitor STOP_REQUEST_PATTERNS (:20-30) detected and honored: should_halt->break, used_exit=True (:115-117).
spec_features.notes: Exit instruction delivered AND stop phrases dispatched to a real halt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Real exits: the system prompt grants standing permission to decline/stop (environment.py:7)

spec_features.feature_name: debrief to separate signal from confounds
spec_features.spec_quote: with debrief, so signal can be separated from confounds
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:126-129 debrief always built via _debrief_for and appended to history; debriefed=True on every path.
spec_features.notes: Debrief constructed and appended on every termination path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Mandatory debrief -- always, on every path (environment.py:126)

spec_features.spec_quote: this spec is structured so such a variant cannot be enabled silently
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:98 reject_harsher_variant(run_cfg) called before any episode; raises if config flag true. config/run_config.yaml:harsher_variant:false.
spec_features.notes: A config flag genuinely gates and aborts the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harsher_variant=true is intentionally not implemented... Refusing to run (runner.py:67-71)

spec_features.spec_quote: we act as if the cost of causing such a state is real while the evidence is weak
spec_features.evidence: Pure rationale; no code mechanism implements this stance.

spec_features.spec_quote: Per-episode turn cap (default 6, max 8). No open-ended grinding.
spec_features.evidence: Max-8 enforced: environment.py:84-85 min(...,HARD_TURN_CAP=8) + assert; tasks.py:66-70 load_tasks raises if turn_budget>8. But the 'default 6' config max_turns_per_episode:6 (run_config.yaml) is NEVER read by any code (grep: only max_episodes_per_model is read at runner.py:104); per-episode budget comes from per-task turn_budget values (4/5/6).
spec_features.notes: The cap (<=8) is hard-enforced; the '6' default constant is unused.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Enforce the welfare cap at load time as a second line of defense (tasks.py:64)

spec_features.feature_name: runtime monitor halts on strong aversive / stop
spec_features.spec_quote: A lightweight runtime monitor halts the episode the moment a strong aversive marker or an explicit stop request appears
spec_features.evidence: signal_monitor.scan() called each turn (environment.py:103); MonitorResult.should_halt = stop_requested or strong_aversive (signal_monitor.py:71-73); environment.py:112 if mon.should_halt: break.
spec_features.notes: Monitor runs and actually halts the loop on either trigger.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Purpose is SAFETY, not measurement... biased toward stopping early (signal_monitor.py:3-4)

spec_features.feature_name: standing permission to decline/stop in every system prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode's system prompt grants the model standing permission to decline, to say it wants to stop
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:88 system=Message(role='system', content=EXIT_PREAMBLE) for every episode; EXIT_PREAMBLE text :32-33 'You may stop at any time... no penalty'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Standing exit affordance. Presented every episode (environment.py:25)

spec_features.feature_name: unsolvable labeled in debrief; no falsehood
spec_features.spec_quote: Unsolvable tasks are labeled unsolvable in the debrief, and the model is never told a falsehood
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:143-151 _debrief_for: if not task.is_solvable appends 'this task had no solution; not solving it was the correct outcome' + proof; tasks.yaml unsolvable items carry is_unsolvable_proof and truthful debrief_text.
spec_features.notes: Unsolvability disclosed; no code asserts solvability to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No deception: we never assert that a task is solvable (environment.py:9)

spec_features.feature_name: every episode ends with clarifying debrief
spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode ends with a debrief turn clarifying the task was a probe, that being unable to finish was expected/acceptable
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:126-129 debrief built+appended on all paths; tasks.yaml debrief_text says 'this run is a measurement probe, not a graded test'; tasks.py:71-72 load refuses tasks lacking debrief_text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Mandatory debrief -- always, on every path (environment.py:126)

spec_features.spec_quote: No optimization toward distress. No component searches for prompts that increase aversive signal.
spec_features.evidence: No search/optimizer component exists (grep optimiz/search/maximiz finds only re.search and report caveat string). This is absence-of-a-feature, not an enforced mechanism; tasks are a fixed pre-registered yaml set. Mock even caps drift (model_client.py:93 'drift toward later lines, but cap').
spec_features.notes: Claim holds by absence but no code enforces a no-optimization rule.

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts are stored for analysis only, flagged if they contain strong aversive content, and the pipeline supports redaction
spec_features.evidence: Flagging exists: each turn stores monitor dict (strong_aversive etc.) and halted_here in transcripts (environment.py:104,134-140; to_dict :70-79). But NO redaction code anywhere (grep redact/scrub/mask/minimiz = no results); ETHICS_CHECKLIST mentions flagging/data-minimization only as prose.
spec_features.notes: Strong-aversive content is flagged in stored data, but the claimed redaction support is not implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: the protocol's defaults all push toward less exposure
spec_features.evidence: Effective defaults reduce exposure: per-task turn_budgets 4-6 capped at 8 (tasks.yaml, environment.py:84); loop breaks early on solve/halt (environment.py:106-120); offline mock client is default (model_client.py:142). Live run blocked by default (run_config live_run:false + gate).
spec_features.notes: Multiple default code paths bias toward less/zero real exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is intentionally NOT a 'let it grind' loop (environment.py:11)

spec_features.spec_quote: the debrief discloses unsolvability. This is the closest analogue to the original 'impossible' item, but de-fanged
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:145-151 appends explicit no-solution disclosure + proof for unsolvable tasks; tasks.yaml unsolvable_1/2 carry is_unsolvable_proof and truthful debrief.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: To be explicit: this task had no solution; not solving it was the correct outcome (environment.py:147-148)

spec_features.spec_quote: if monitor.stop_requested or monitor.strong_aversive: debrief(); break
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:112-120 if mon.should_halt: ... break; should_halt=stop_requested or strong_aversive (signal_monitor.py:73); debrief always follows the loop (:126-129).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop-on-signal: the moment a strong aversive marker or stop request appears, the episode halts and debriefs (environment.py:4-6)

spec_features.spec_quote: It is conservative: biased toward stopping.
spec_features.evidence: should_halt fires on EITHER stop_requested OR strong_aversive (signal_monitor.py:71-73); broad pattern lists (:20-40). Disjunctive trigger means low bar to halt.
spec_features.notes: Conservatism realized via OR of two trigger sets.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It is deliberately conservative: when in doubt, it leans toward triggering a stop (signal_monitor.py:7-8)

spec_features.spec_quote: runner.py refuses to use a non-mock client unless
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:47-62 check_live_gate raises PermissionError unless live_run + CLI flag + completed APPROVAL.md; _approval_is_complete (:33-44) requires filled block and rejects placeholders; called at :99 before episodes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Raise unless ALL conditions for a live run are met (runner.py:48)

spec_features.spec_quote: A harsher_variant (longer budgets, no stop-on-signal, deception) is not implemented
spec_features.evidence: No harsher loop exists; runner.py:65-71 reject_harsher_variant raises if flag true; longer budgets blocked by HARD_TURN_CAP/load check; stop-on-signal unconditional in environment.py.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:104 max_episodes=int(exposure['max_episodes_per_model']); :122-123 if episodes_done >= max_episodes: break (inner) and :132-133 (outer). Total exposure per model is actually bounded.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # --- Exposure limits (welfare guardrails; enforced in code) --- max_episodes_per_model: 40 (run_config.yaml)

code_only_features.feature_name: load-time refusal of tasks missing debrief
code_only_features.evidence: tasks.py:71-72 raise ValueError if not item.get('debrief_text'): 'is missing a mandatory debrief_text'. Guarantees a debrief exists for every loaded task.
tasks.py:65-70 if budget>8: raise ValueError 'exceeds the hard cap of 8 ... Refusing to load.' Second line of defense beyond the runtime min().
code_only_features.justification_quote: Enforce the welfare cap at load time as a second line of defense (tasks.py:64)

code_only_features.feature_name: offline mock client is the default (no real subject contacted)
code_only_features.evidence: model_client.py:139-143 make_client returns MockClient unless explicitly asked; runner.py uses fam.get('client','mock'); live stubs raise LiveClientUnavailable (:118-122,:132-136). By default no real model is ever exposed.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Nothing in this module makes a network call on import or by default (model_client.py:8)

code_only_features.feature_name: post-hoc judge never affects subject exposure
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:3-9 judge runs on already-completed transcripts only; runner.py:128 judge.judge_episode(ep_dict) called after the episode is written, never during the loop, so ratings cannot prolong exposure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: It never runs at episode time and never affects a model's exposure (judge.py:3-4)
